2: A Prayer of the afflicted when he is feeble, and before Jehovah poureth out his plaint. O Jehovah, hear my prayer, yea, my cry to Thee cometh.
3: Hide not Thou Thy face from me, In a day of mine adversity, Incline unto me Thine ear, In the day I call, haste, answer me.
4: For consumed in smoke have been my days, And my bones as a fire-brand have burned.
5: Smitten as the herb, and withered, is my heart, For I have forgotten to eat my bread.
6: From the voice of my sighing Hath my bone cleaved to my flesh.
7: I have been like to a pelican of the wilderness, I have been as an owl of the dry places.
8: I have watched, and I am As a bird alone on the roof.
9: All the day mine enemies reproached me, Those mad at me have sworn against me.
10: Because ashes as bread I have eaten, And my drink with weeping have mingled,
11: From Thine indignation and Thy wrath, For Thou hast lifted me up, And dost cast me down.
12: My days as a shadow are stretched out, And I--as the herb I am withered.
13: And Thou, O Jehovah, to the age abidest, And Thy memorial to all generations.
14: Thou--Thou risest--Thou pitiest Zion, For the time to favour her, For the appointed time hath come.
15: For Thy servants have been pleased with her stones, And her dust they favour.
16: And nations fear the name of Jehovah, And all kings of the earth Thine honour,
17: For Jehovah hath builded Zion, He hath been seen in His honour,
18: He turned unto the prayer of the destitute, And He hath not despised their prayer.
19: This is written for a later generation, And the people created do praise Jah.
20: For He hath looked From the high place of His sanctuary. Jehovah from heaven unto earth looked attentively,
21: To hear the groan of the prisoner, To loose sons of death,
22: To declare in Zion the name of Jehovah, And His praise in Jerusalem,
23: In the peoples being gathered together, And the kingdoms--to serve Jehovah.
24: He hath humbled in the way my power, He hath shortened my days.
25: I say, `My God, take me not up in the midst of my days,' Through all generations are Thine years.
26: Beforetime the earth Thou didst found, And the work of Thy hands are the heavens.
27: They--They perish, and Thou remainest, And all of them as a garment become old, As clothing Thou changest them, And they are changed.
28: And Thou art the same, and Thine years are not finished.
29: The sons of Thy servants do continue, And their seed before Thee is established!
